title: Return a greeting
description: Implement Hello so it returns a friendly greeting for the provided name: Hello("Chris") -> "Hello, Chris". If the name is empty, greet World instead: Hello("") -> "Hello, World".
objective: Practice defining a function, using strings, and returning values.

metadata.source: Learn Go With Tests - Hello, world

title: Add two integers
description: Implement Add so it returns the sum of two integers: Add(2, 3) -> 5.
objective: Practice integer parameters, return types, and simple arithmetic.

title: Repeat a string
description: Implement Repeat so it returns the provided character repeated count times: Repeat("a", 5) -> "aaaaa". A count of 0 returns an empty string: Repeat("b", 0) -> "".
objective: Practice for loops and string concatenation.

title: Sum a slice
description: Implement Sum so it returns the total of every integer in the provided slice: Sum([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]) -> 15. An empty slice returns 0: Sum([]) -> 0.
objective: Practice slices, range loops, and accumulation.

metadata.source: Learn Go With Tests - Arrays and slices

title: Calculate rectangle area
description: Define an Area method on Rectangle that returns width multiplied by height: Rectangle(width: 12, height: 6).Area() -> 72.

metadata.source: Learn Go With Tests - Structs, methods and interfaces

title: Test a doubling function
description: A function called Double is already implemented. It returns twice the provided integer: Double(4) -> 8, Double(-3) -> -6. Write a test that verifies this behavior.
objective: Practice writing a basic Go test that calls a function, checks its result, and reports failure with t.Errorf or t.Fatalf.
mutant_hints: returns the number unchanged instead of doubling it
always returns zero instead of doubling the number

metadata.source: Learn Go With Tests - Writing tests

title: Test a sign-reporting function
description: A function called Sign is already implemented. It reports whether a number is positive, negative, or zero: Sign(5) -> "positive", Sign(-5) -> "negative", Sign(0) -> "zero". Write a test that checks all three cases, including zero.
objective: Practice table-driven Go tests that cover multiple cases, including an edge case.
mutant_hints: misreports zero as positive instead of zero
misreports zero as negative instead of zero

metadata.source: Learn Go With Tests - Writing tests

title: Test FizzBuzz with named subtests
description: A function called FizzBuzz is already implemented. For a number divisible by 3 it returns Fizz: FizzBuzz(3) -> "Fizz". For a number divisible by 5 it returns Buzz: FizzBuzz(5) -> "Buzz". For a number divisible by both it returns FizzBuzz: FizzBuzz(15) -> "FizzBuzz". Otherwise it returns the number itself as text: FizzBuzz(2) -> "2". Write a table-driven test with a named subtest for each case using t.Run.
objective: Practice organizing table-driven test cases into named subtests with t.Run.
mutant_hints: returns Fizz instead of FizzBuzz for numbers divisible by both 3 and 5
does not treat multiples of 5 as Buzz
returns an empty string instead of the number itself for values not divisible by 3 or 5
